name: animism

attributes.attribute: a place-bound, polytheistic belief in living spirit
had spirits that stayed within their own waters

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Animism is a religious concept. The Celts filled the world with spirit, as did many ancient peoples. It did not take one single, abstract god of nature. It was bound to place and it was polytheistic: it had many gods. A startling outcrop of rock might hold a goddess, and a great old tree a god. Such gods were often known only in one place. The spirits of wells did not wander to meet far tribes. They stayed inside their own sacred waters. This animism may have begun with pre-Celtic peoples. It later became part of the Celtic Christian tradition. See also the genius loci.
objective: Record animism, the Celtic belief in living spirit.
